        How to use
        Item Filters

            v1.0

         by Colonel"

"Introduction

Hello! This book acts as a guide for the item filter system.

Firstly, filters are crafted through a smithing table. You need 1 hopper, 1 paper, and 1 dye. Use a recipe viewer for more info!"

"Introduction

There are two ways in which you can update a filter:
• Filter Addition
• Field Adjustment 

To put it simply: If you're editing some filter value, it's a field adjustment. If you're adding a sub-filter, it's an addition. "

"Filter Addition

Take one filter (the base) and add a second filter (the sacrifice) to the crafting grid in the following shape:

██ 

The base goes on the left, the sacrifice on the right. "

"Field Adjustment

Field adjustment is a two-step process:

1) Add the field to the filter through the book editor (write it in the book).

2) Put the filter through a crafting table to apply the field adjustment."

"Field Adjustment

The fields are name-value pairs joined by '='. Ex: The following sets the mode to "None":
mode=none

Note: All modes are specified like that. 

Fields are case-insensitive."

"Field Adjustment

You can specify multiple fields at once. Add a blank line between each field you want to enter.

You can use multiple pages to enter fields, but a field cannot span multiple pages."

"Unpacking

If you add a sub-filter to a filter and later want to undo that, you can sneak while right clicking with the filter to unpack it.

This is required if you want to replace a sub-filter with a different one."

"Applying

To apply a filter to a copper pipe, simply right click the pipe while holding the filter in your main hand slot.

This works for finalized as well as unfinalized filters."

"Finalizing

When you're done modifying your filter, you have the option to finalize it by signing it and giving it a name.

Note: If you do this, you can no longer edit the filter, so be careful! Also, this prevents unpacking!"

"Content Filter

Filters shulkers and bundles based on their contents.

'slot' is a whole number greater than 0. Examples:
• slot=1
• slot=27

Modes are specified on the next page."

"Content Filter

'Any', 'All', and 'None' pass based on if any, all, or none of the container items match the sub-filter.

'Empty' passes if the container is empty. 'Specific': Passes if the nth slot (starting at 1) passes the sub-filter."

"Content Filter

Shulker boxes include empty slots i.e slot=27 points to the last slot.

The 'All' mode fails on empty containers. 

Unspecified sub-filter always passes.

Swapping sub-filter requires unpacking."

"Durability Filter

Filters based on durability as a percentage. Ex:
value=12.3%
value=26

Allowed modes are:
• At least
• At most

Items without durability always fail."

"Enchantment Filter

Filters based on enchantments. Also works with enchanted books!

Allowed modes are:
• At least
• At most
• Exact"

"Enchantment Filter

To specify the enchantment, you need the target ID. Ex:
enchant=mending
enchant=minecraft:wow
enchant=enderscape:rebound

Level is specified as a whole number. Ex:
level=0
level=4"

"Group Filter

Combines multiple filters into one.

Allowed modes are:
• Any
• All
• None

Sub-filters are added through filter addition and can later be all unpacked at once."

"Name Filter

Filters based on normal or renamed item name.

Allowed modes are:
• Contains
• Starts with
• Ends with
• Exact"

"Name Filter

Set the searched value as a string, i.e:
value=red 
value=pickaxe

Optionally, toggle case sensitivity with:
sensitive=true
sensitive=false"

"Tag Filter

Filters based on which tags item has. Use an item viewer for tags!

Allowed modes are:
• Any
• All
• None

To add/remove tags:
tag=dirt
tag=#c:buckets"

"Type Filter

Filters based on item type. Allowed modes:
• Any
• None

To add/remove types, use the identifier, i.e:
item=stone
item=minecraft:dirt"

"Tips and Tricks

A finalized filter can be duplicated just like a normal book.

Group / Content filters can be nested for more combinations.

A group filter with mode 'none' works as an inverter for one supplied sub-filter.
"

"Conclusion

I hope this book was helpful to you.

If you have any questions, comments, or concerns, let me know, and I'll try to improve in the next version!

-Colonel"
